title: Handling an export request for a single account
notes: A support-driven export question that touches both customer rows while working out which accounts are special.

markers: finance still checks the refund path

turns.text: Support has a customer asking for their full invoice history as a file. Is there a supported way to do that or do we do it by hand?
I will find out what the service offers today, and whether any account is already handled differently, because if there is a precedent it is probably the answer.

There is a precedent, and it is explicit. One account is rejected by the invoice listing outright with a 409 telling it to use the nightly export instead, because it is on a bespoke contract from a renewal and pulls its whole ledger that way. So a full-history export path exists, it is just not reachable through this API.

turns.result: app.py:35:# renewal and pulls its whole ledger through the nightly export instead.

turns.text: The only mention in this repository is that comment. The export itself lives somewhere else, which means support cannot self-serve it from anything we own here.
The listing endpoint serialises to JSON with amounts converted from cents, so anything built on it would produce JSON rather than the spreadsheet a customer probably expects.

The fixtures are informative here too. One row is annotated as retained from a reconciliation, with a note that finance checks the refund path against it by hand. So there is already a manual, human process attached to specific accounts, running alongside the automated one.
so is by-hand actually the normal thing here?
It appears to be, for anything that does not fit the default shape. Two different accounts have bespoke handling, one encoded in the application and one encoded in a test fixture and a finance habit.

If an export were built here it would go through this helper, which limits in SQL and retries on connection failure. A full-history export for a large account is exactly the kind of query that would sit at the edge of that retry behaviour — slow enough to fail, retried three times, making it slower still.
so building it here would be a bad idea?

Building it as a synchronous HTTP endpoint would be. The existing answer of a nightly export exists for a reason, and that reason is visible in the code: reads go to a replica, the replica lags, and a big read during lag is the worst case for both the reader and everyone else on that replica.

The listing endpoint is designed around small paged reads — a customer id, a bounded limit, an ordered query. An export is the opposite shape, and grafting it onto this endpoint would mean carrying its constraints for no reason.
The configured page size is a small default with a hard ceiling above it in the handler, which reinforces the point: everything about this endpoint assumes bounded reads.
And the handler has barely changed since the initial import, so the special-cased account has been handled that way for most of the service's life rather than as a recent workaround.

My answer to support: there is no supported self-serve export in this service. The nightly export exists outside it and one account is already routed to it deliberately. The honest options are to route this customer the same way, or to build an export endpoint properly — and the second is worth doing, because the number of accounts with hand-maintained special handling is now at least two and each one is invisible until someone reads the source.
